summary: Tested the BR phone 9th-digit normalization and the Trevo da Sorte raffle on the backend and the frontend. Backend: 15 of 15 pytest tests pass. They cover _clean, normalize_phone, br_variants, the legacy-row upgrade in find_or_create_customer (using a temp row), the public trial 400 for a short number, raffle auth and public access, settings persistence, the 400 for drawing with no clovers, and perform_draw with mocked renewal and notifier (a temp payment with 3 clovers plus a joker gives a pool of 4, the winner is placed at win_index, renewal and admin alert are called once, a second draw is blocked, and history is filled). Frontend: the /sorteio stats, settings save and reload, disabled draw button and history all work. The /pay/227470206 clover picker is checked by default with 1 clover. Plus and minus change the count (capped at 10), unchecking drops the clover cost (R$32 → R$30), and the totals are correct (R$30 + 1×R$2 = R$32,00, 3 clovers = R$36,00). The picker is hidden when the raffle is disabled. The mobile layout is OK. All test data was cleaned up and the raffle was reset to disabled.

critical.issue: Participant names will show as numeric painel IDs. The query uses LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.id = p.customer_id, but payments.customer_id is the painel user id (e.g. 228245283), not customers.id. In the DB, 0 of the 171 distinct payment customer_ids match a customers.id. So the name falls back to str(customer_id) in the admin entries list, the DrawReel sequence, the winner WhatsApp message ('Parabéns, 228245283!'), the admin alert, history and public last_winner. Fix: get the username from the painel cache (routers.payments._cache_user / painel_users._read_cache) by customer_id.

minor.issue: The prize renewal always uses painel.get_package_id('iptv', months), whatever the winner's real system type is (p2p/dreamtv users could get the wrong package).

If anything fails between inserting the lock doc and update_one (e.g. _resolve_joker raising because the cache read fails), the raffle_draws doc stays at status='drawing'. The month is then permanently blocked and nothing appears in history, because history only shows status='drawn'. Wrap the code in try/except and delete or mark the lock as failed.

The pool reads only local SQLite payments. Any env that shares Atlas but has a stale SQLite would draw from a different pool. Only the env that holds the real payments (the Raspberry) should run auto_draw_loop.

If a caller passes the legacy 12-digit form while a canonical row exists, the row would be rewritten to the legacy form. Current callers normalize first, so this is safe today but fragile. Also, existing duplicate customer rows (12-digit and 13-digit for the same person) are not merged; only new lookups upgrade.
